Complete risk signal-extraction offline core (session 10E)

Harden pipeline/signals.py prototype + add deterministic attribution,
history (occurrence/episode/quiet-cycle), calendar (C1 countdown), and
the extraction prompt. 1265 tests pass; 5 backtest scenario scores
reproduce exactly (100.0/63.9/100.0/87.3/8.1). Scorer + weights untouched.

Add risk signal-extraction plan (session 10D)

Astra-authored plan: LLM classification + deterministic field derivation,
scoring stays deterministic. Reuses offline pipeline/signals.py prototype.
Gated on 5 backtests + 5 hand-labeled histories + budget.

Remove mistral batch_size floor; restore understand to batch 5

mistral's batch_size: 2 floored the whole understand loop via
effective_batch_size(), so 150 clusters needed 75 calls against the
70-call budget -> 52 cap_refused clusters (run 36123832881). Mistral's
batch-5 omission (~50%) is already recovered by the batch-element retry
in batch_run.py (minimal 6-field contract), so the floor is redundant.
Remove it: mistral inherits the global batch 5, understand drops to 30
calls, and the budget covers all 150 clusters plus retries.

fix(understand): minimal recovery contract for ministral batch omissions

ministral-8b flaked on the array form and dumped bare entity-name
lists against the heavy 8-field understand.txt (live 2026-09-24:
12/43 mistral clusters lost). Retry each omitted batch element once
with a minimal 6-field contract (no nested entities/why_matters),
the one shape probe_mistral.py proved it follows.

Also relabel content-filtered retries (clickbait/irrelevant) as
correct drops instead of unavailable, and check the content filter
before the bounds gate in recovery_payload (parity with
process_element).

1014 tests pass.

fix(understand): recover omitted/malformed batch elements via single-object retry

ministral-8b answers one strict JSON object reliably but flakes on the
array-of-objects form (live 2026-09-24 run: 4/6 batches were non-object
elements, losing 8 of 12 served clusters). When a batch element is missing
or non-object, retry that cluster ONCE with the single-object contract via
the existing recovery_payload path (same mechanism as language-drift).

Also log the type+repr of non-object elements so the raw failure shape is
calibratable from the run log, not just the 'not an object' count.

Tests: 2 old cases rewritten + 1 new (recovery success x2, recovery failure),
full suite 1011 passed.

fix(understand): per-provider batch_size floors mistral to 2

ministral-8b omits ~50% of clusters per call at the shared batch_size=5
(retest 36051610488: 40/80 'missing from response array'; tokens_out
910-1382 vs max_tokens 2000, so NOT truncation -- it answers but stops
early). Add optional per-provider batch_size; effective_batch_size()
floors the understand loop to the smallest cascade provider's value, so
a batch the router fails over to mistral stays legal for it.

- settings_llm: ProviderSettings.batch_size + effective_batch_size()
- settings_guard: reject provider batch_size < 1
- pipeline: UnderstandStage + batch-template load use effective value
- settings.yaml: mistral batch_size 2; groq/groq2/gemini keep 5
fix(understand): salvage wrapped/prose-wrapped batch arrays; precise parse reasons

fix(observability): drop redundant provider-status from fate reason column

result.status already IS the fate value for unavailable/timeout fates, so
writing it again into the reason column was duplicate. Provider-fail detail
stays run-log-only per the documented contract; reason is reserved for
deterministic contract-gate causes (oversized word count, parse error).

fix(prellm): cross-host redirect auth + three-bucket calibration semantics

- download_run_reports.py: follow the artifact zip's 302 to Azure Blob
  without the Authorization header (urllib forwards it cross-host, Azure
  rejects it -> 401). Skip only when a run dir actually has CSV content.
- prellm_calibration.py: keep_lost now counts only sent-producing fates
  (sent/sent_followup/lead_only). repeat/cap/oversized/rank/lang/relevance/
  unparseable are a third "dropped-anyway" bucket -- never sent, so a
  threshold removing them early is budget savings, not a lost story. The
  prior "keep = not waste" made recommend() too conservative against the
  real 45%+ waste / ~40% dropped-anyway mix.
- tests: three-bucket separation + dropped-anyway-not-a-loss coverage.
997 passed.

feat(understand): optional 'why it matters' context line (owner 2026-09-06)

Adds an OPTIONAL one-sentence background line to the digest, rendered as a
«چرا مهم است:» footer distinct from reported facts. Anti-hallucination fence:
the prompt forbids any date/number/quote/name absent from the source and
instructs omit-rather-than-guess; the parser TRIMS (never gates) the field --
empty or over-long context drops, the event's facts survive. Zero extra LLM
calls. In-memory only, not persisted.

docs(brief): record data-grounded rejection of fragmentation hypothesis

Run 35712130649 (post-Session-17, 150-cap): 51 same-run pairs, 0 fragments,
max cosine 0.63; cross-run repeat gate dropped 25 near-dups via its two-band
+ score-floor logic; 24 delivered items all distinct. D1 settled: leave the
0.80 threshold, do not add a same-run two-band.

fix(ci): upload run-reports even on failure/timeout

A near-timeout run still writes its pairs_*.csv dedup log, but the
upload step (no if:always()) silently drops it on failure -- hiding the
fragmentation signal exactly when the run is most worth diagnosing.
Matches the state-backup step's convention.

feat(tools): add pairs_*.csv fragmentation analyzer

Parses the same-run pair log into the D1 measurement: kept-below-threshold
pairs split by novelty (fragment = same story should have merged vs
development = legitimately distinct), bucketed by cosine similarity. Settles
whether the 0.80 threshold should move or whether cosine alone cannot
separate paraphrase (needs the two-band/content-novelty logic).

Companion to b850767 (the novelty field this analyzer keys on).

feat(pipeline): tag same-run pairs with novelty (development vs fragment)

Adds a 'novelty' field to PairRecord and pairs_<ts>.csv, reusing
repeat_decision._content_novelty to mark each logged pair as either
'development' (one side brings a new number/entity the other lacks) or
'fragment' (same story, should have merged). This turns the existing
pairwise-cosine log into the measurement the fragmentation decision needs,
with zero LLM calls and no drop-logic change.

Analysis-time filter: count decision=kept_below_threshold AND
novelty=fragment for true fragmentation; development pairs are legitimately
distinct. See agents/briefs/SESSION_21_BRIEF.md.

fix(llm): export MISTRAL_API_KEY in pipeline run env

Mistral was wired (509efca) but never fired in production: the Run pipeline
step didn't export MISTRAL_API_KEY, so build_adapters skipped it every run
(log: 'no MISTRAL_API_KEY in environment'). The secret exists (probe-mistral
uses it). Also fix List-Groq-models step mapping GROQ_API_KEY_2 to the wrong
secret.

fix(understand): state the contract's summary bounds in the prompt

Mistral (ministral-8b) writes 68-70-word summaries that the contract
rejects at SUMMARY_WORD_BOUNDS=(2,60). The prompt only said '2-3 short
sentences' -- no numeric cap -- so the model obeyed the prompt and was
punished for it. Both understand.txt and understand_batch.txt now state
'2 to 60 words (never empty)', matching the contract exactly.

feat(extract): signal-extraction unit (offline-measurable) + gate tests

unit before wiring, so the accuracy gate has something to score.

- src/agent/pipeline/signals.py: extract() makes one router call/cluster,
  validates signal_id against the catalog (C1 + G1/G2 excluded), parses
  event_date (ISO date/datetime, fallback to cluster date), and returns
  ExtractedSignal records + attribute_signal_event() bridge to the
  deterministic engine. Not wired into build_stages (deferred until
  measured accuracy + token cost).
- tests/unit/test_pipeline_signals.py: 13 gate tests (stub router, no LLM).

fix(langgate): soft ي/ك markers need count>=2 — stop false drops of corroborated items

Quality round (run 34872885506): a single Arabic yeh U+064A in the
transliteration 'بتسيلم' (B'Tselem) tripped is_persian_output and
lang_dropped the run's only corroborated 'likely' item (score 12.04,
2 sources). Persian LLM output routinely carries one stray ي/ك in
foreign names, so dropping on a single occurrence biased the gate
against exactly the international multi-source stories it must keep.

Split markers: STRONG (ة ى إ + Hebrew) any-occurrence drop; SOFT (ي ك)
drop only at count>=2. Monotonic — recovers single-ي items, never adds
a drop. langretry shares the contract.

Also raise max_clusters_per_run 40->55 (was cap_dropping a relevant
Reuters Hormuz item even on a quiet day). Suite 849 -> 851.

fix(llm): safety-factor the token pacer to stop groq 429 thrash

Run 34846355119 still 429'd 4 of 11 groq calls. Every 429 was a
request fired <320ms after the previous one (back-to-back), which the
estimate allowed because two small batches fit under the nominal 8,000.
groq rejected at 5.4-6.1K ACTUAL tokens -- well under 8K -- so the
nominal TPM overstates the effective limit (rejected requests consume
the window; the coarse chars/3.0 estimate under-measures token-dense
Persian). Book against 65% of nominal TPM; the overfit check stays
against the full nominal so a single batch never re-triggers the old
sending-anyway thrash.
